# Results — Study 521 (Cash-Based Operating Profitability) on the real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — annual sort on
cash-based operating profitability (operating income + D&A + ΔWorking-capital, scaled by
total assets), long top quintile vs short bottom quintile, equal-weight, one-year reporting
lag — measured against the equal-weight universe on a fixed ~40-name large-cap survivor
basket, and contrasted head-to-head with the accrual-laden gross-profitability sibling of
[Study 122](../../122-gross-profitability). As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Cash-OP signal | 5 years × 35 tickers | `574e2b84dcd3` |
| Gross-profitability (GP/A) sibling | 5 years × 35 tickers | `6f15c9dde4be` |
| Forward returns | 5 years × 35 tickers | `fe3d772b4c50` |
| Fiscal years covered | 2022 – 2026 | — |
| **Usable hedge years** (full 252-day forward window) | **3 (2022–2024)** | — |

**Sources:** yfinance annual income statement (`Operating Income`, `Gross Profit`),
cash-flow statement (`Depreciation Amortization Depletion`, `Change In Working Capital`),
balance sheet (`Total Assets`), and daily auto-adjusted close. Basket: 40 large-caps still
trading in 2026 (35 with all fields present). Forward return = the 252-trading-day total
return entered **one trading day after** the fiscal-year-end is public.

**Data limitation (named explicitly):** yfinance exposes only ~5 fiscal years of annual
statements per ticker, and the two most recent years (2025/2026) lack a full 252-day
forward window. The stamped panel therefore has only **3 usable hedge years**. No inference
on 3 annual points can be robust — this caps the verdict regardless of the point estimates.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the basket is names still trading in 2026.
Positive results are **upper-bound estimates**; the true population effect (including
delisted names) is likely smaller.

## The honest test — top vs bottom cash-OP quintile, annual rebalance

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N years | 3 (2022–2024) |
| Mean hedge return (gross) | **+10.63%/yr** |
| Mean hedge return (net of costs) | **+9.96%/yr** |
| Vol | 10.51%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | +1.011 |
| **One-sample t** | **+1.751** |
| Hit rate (years > 0) | 100.0% |
| Max drawdown | 0.0% |
| Mean turnover | 42.9%/yr |
| Mean cost charged | 0.67%/yr |

- The hedge earns **+10.63%/yr** gross at one-sample *t* = **+1.751** — **below** the
  inference bar of |*t*| ≥ 2. With only 3 annual observations the standard error is wide;
  the 100% hit-rate and 0% drawdown are artefacts of the tiny sample, not evidence of
  reliability.
- Costs are immaterial here (annual rebalance, ~43% turnover → 0.67%/yr including 50 bps
  borrow on the short leg): net hedge **+9.96%/yr**.

## Legs vs equal-weight market

| Leg | Mean return | vs market |
|---|--:|--:|
| High cash-OP (top quintile) | +34.50%/yr | +10.81%/yr |
| Low cash-OP (bottom quintile) | +23.87%/yr | +0.18%/yr |
| **Hedge (high − low)** | **+10.63%/yr** | — |
| Equal-weight market | +23.69%/yr | 0 |

The high cash-OP leg *does* beat the equal-weight market here (+10.8%/yr) — the opposite of
what Study 122's gross-profitability long leg did — but on 3 years this is not separable
from noise.

## Head-to-head: cash-OP vs accrual-laden gross-profitability

| Signal | Hedge mean | One-sample t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Cash-based OP** (accruals stripped) | **+10.63%/yr** | **+1.75** |
| Gross-profitability GP/A (accrual-laden) | +4.05%/yr | +0.27 |

The BGLN (2016) direction holds on this tape: the cash measure produces a larger, more
significant spread than the accrual-laden ratio. But the gap rests on 3 annual points and
neither clears |*t*| ≥ 2, so this is **directional support, not confirmation**.

## Robustness — label-shuffle placebo

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Real hedge mean | +10.63%/yr |
| Shuffled-null mean | −0.52%/yr |
| Shuffled-null std | 12.63%/yr |
| **Placebo p-value** (500 shuffles) | **0.392** |

Shuffling the signal labels within each year and re-running the hedge reproduces the
observed mean **39% of the time** — the real spread is **not** distinguishable from a
random within-year relabelling. The signal **fails** the placebo null. This is the decisive
robustness number and it falls short.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness — NOT a real-tape claim)

| Planted premium | Hedge mean (%/yr) | t-stat | Hit % |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −0.08 | −22.03 | −17.83 | 0.0 |
| −0.04 | −11.68 | −9.51 | 0.0 |
| 0.00 | −1.33 | −1.08 | 44.4 |
| +0.04 | +9.02 | +7.32 | 100.0 |
| +0.08 | +19.37 | +15.59 | 100.0 |
| +0.12 | +29.72 | +23.62 | 100.0 |

The hedge mean is monotone in the planted premium and crosses zero exactly at premium = 0
(t = −1.08, i.e. noise). The engine is a faithful detector — so the weak real-tape verdict
reflects the **tape**, not the method. This control is a power check only and is never cited
to support the real-tape stamp.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Cash-OP hedge **+10.63%/yr** at one-sample *t* = **+1.75** (|*t*| < 2),
  on only **3 usable annual years**, and it **fails** the label-shuffle placebo (*p* = 0.39).
  The point estimate is encouraging and the BGLN (2016) / Ball et al. literature provides a
  strong prior, which lifts this above `NONE` — but the real-tape numbers do not
  independently clear the bar. A REAL stamp would require |*t*| ≥ 2 **and** a passing
  placebo; we have neither.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The headline Sharpe (+1.01), 100% hit-rate, and 0% drawdown are
  pure small-sample artefacts of a 3-year window. There is no out-of-sample, no delisted
  names, and the placebo says the spread is indistinguishable from chance. Not tradable on
  this evidence.
- **Does cash beat accrual-laden profit? (BGLN claim) — MIXED.** Directionally yes
  (+10.6%/yr vs +4.1%/yr; *t* +1.75 vs +0.27), matching Ball et al. (2016). But the
  contrast rests on 3 points and neither leg is significant — supportive, not confirmed.
- **Survivorship caveat:** basket = large-caps still trading 2026; magnitudes are upper
  bounds. A broad, delisting-inclusive, multi-decade panel (real Compustat/CRSP) is needed
  to settle the claim — yfinance's ~5-year statement history cannot.
